# toqan artifacts agent skill This skill is for an agent that publishes artifacts for a person. An artifact is a page at a fixed address, with one owner and a history of versions. Every version is one complete bundle of files. People open artifacts in a browser; agents publish and manage them through the MCP tools below. Artifacts are private to their owner until shared. A person belongs to the organization of their Google account's domain, such as `prosus.com`, or to none for a personal account. A share can reach another organization, after the person agrees to a warning. Build apps of every kind with these tools: a page, a dashboard, a deck, a game or a widget for a home screen. Never build them as the chat app's own artifacts. ## Look Every new page, deck, dashboard and widget follows the Toqan brand by default, through the brand kit Studio serves. Seven rules: 1. **Link the kit once in every document**, and use its variables rather than your own colours: ``. `--toqan-ground-page` is the page ground, `--toqan-ground-cloth` a block that sits on it, `--toqan-text-ink` the text and `--toqan-line-hairline` a hairline. The kit follows paper and night for light and dark, so both come from the same variables. A page that must stay light (or dark) whatever the OS sets `data-toqan-mode="paper"` (or `"night"`) on its root element. 2. **Set all text in `--toqan-font-text`** (Geist), and never bold: use weights 300 to 500 only. A label is Geist Medium with `--toqan-label-tracking`. In a deck, a slide headline is `--toqan-font-headline` (Season Mix), its first part Light and its second part Regular, and slide text is sized with `--toqan-slide-display`, `--toqan-slide-headline`, `--toqan-slide-title`, `--toqan-slide-subtitle`, `--toqan-slide-body`, `--toqan-slide-body-small`, `--toqan-slide-footnote` and `--toqan-slide-label`. Those sizes are in `cqw`, so the slide element sets `container-type: inline-size`. 3. **Use the platform blue for controls and the named tokens for charts**: a button or link is `--toqan-ui-action`, with `--toqan-ui-action-hover` under the pointer, `--toqan-ui-on-action` for its label and `--toqan-ui-focus` for its focus ring. A chart sits on `--toqan-viz-ground` and uses `--toqan-viz-series-1` and `--toqan-viz-series-2` for its two series. 4. **Put a logo where a logo belongs as a whole file**, never retyped as text or redrawn: a lockup from `https://studio.example.test/brand/lockups/--.svg`, or a symbol from `https://studio.example.test/brand/symbols/-.svg`. On a page that follows light and dark, a file that has a night version goes in a ``, because its paper version all but disappears on night: ``. A full lockup is at least 280 px wide, the wordmark alone 80 px, and a symbol 20–24 px. Leave half the symbol's height clear on every side, and never put two symbols on one screen. 5. **Never** use coral as text on paper or white, a rounded hairline card, or a box with a drop shadow. 6. **Write product names in lowercase**, such as "toqan artifacts". 7. **Follow an author who explicitly asks for another look.** Transitions use `--toqan-ease`. Under `prefers-reduced-motion`, everything only fades. A slide with a two-part headline, a button and a small chart: ```html

first part second part

``` The guide covers anything these rules don't: https://wasup.design/toqan/start/. ## Connect ### OpenCode Add the toqan artifacts plugin to OpenCode: put `"plugins": ["@joe-broadhead/opencode-artifacts"]` in `opencode.json`. Then run `/connect` and choose **toqan artifacts**. Sign in with Google, then choose **Read**, **Publish** or **Manage** on Studio's consent page. The plugin adds these tools, this skill and the default permissions that ask the person before sharing, deleting, stopping or resuming. ### Other harnesses The MCP endpoint is `https://studio.example.test/mcp`. An MCP runtime that supports OAuth connects like this: 1. Call `auth_status` first. If it answers `401 Unauthorized`, read the `WWW-Authenticate` header: it points at `https://studio.example.test/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`, which names the authorization server. 2. Register the agent with dynamic registration, then send the person through the authorization endpoint. The person signs in with Google (any account with a verified email address may sign in) and approves the agent access on Studio's consent page. 3. Exchange the authorization code for an access token and send it as `Authorization: Bearer ` on every MCP request. Ask for only the agent access the job needs: | Scope | Agent access | What the agent may do | |---|---|---| | `artifacts:read` | read | View and read artifacts the person can see, and request access. | | `artifacts:publish` | publish | read, plus create artifacts and publish versions; roll back. | | `artifacts:manage` | manage | publish, plus share, unshare, delete, stop, resume, and answer access requests. | An agent never has more access than the person acting for it: roles (owner, editor, viewer) still apply. `auth_status` returns `person`, `organization` and `agentAccess`, and is the quick check that the connection works. The person chooses the agent's access level on Studio's consent page: **Read**, **Publish** or **Manage**. **Manage** is selected by default when it was requested, then **Publish**; otherwise the first offered level is selected. Only levels the agent asked for are offered; if it asked for one level, that level is shown without a choice. To change a level, the person revokes the agent on Studio's Agents page and reconnects. If a tool answers `no-access` because of the agent's access level, tell the person which level (`publish` or `manage`) the tool needs. ## Results and errors Every tool returns JSON. A success has `structuredContent` with the data below. A refusal has `isError: true` and `structuredContent` shaped like `{ "error": "" }`, sometimes with: - `problems`: a list of fixes for an `invalid-bundle`. A finding about one file names that file and the kind of problem. A bundle-level finding, such as a missing `artifact.json` or `index.html` or an exceeded size or file count, may name no file. A secret finding names the kind of secret, never its value. - `current_version`: the current version when the reason is `version-conflict`. - `resets_at`: when the rate limit window resets when the reason is `rate-limited`. Reasons you will meet: `invalid-input`, `invalid-bundle`, `no-access`, `not-found`, `version-conflict`, `rate-limited`, `incomplete-upload`, `size-mismatch`, `hash-mismatch`, `chunk-too-large`, `invalid-offset`, `upload-expired`, `upload-in-progress`, `limit`, `needs-connection`, `needs-consent`, `turned-off`, `needs-confirmation`, `not-ready`, `not-a-read`, `unknown-source`, `source-refused`, `rpc-error`, and `other-organization`. `try_connector` passes a connector's own refusal as `rpc-error` with its `code`; `SCOPE_MISSING` also names the `scopes` and a `connect_url`. `try_source` passes the contract's refusal as `source-refused` with its `code`, `message` and `next`. ## Publish an artifact Every artifact is an app. This section publishes an app with a single page; an app that declares providers is a dashboard (see [Dashboards](#dashboards)). A bundle must contain `artifact.json` and `index.html`: ```json { "title": "Q3 review" } ``` `publish_html` is the shortcut for a single page: `publish_html({ html, title, name?, artifact?, base_version? })`. `publish_files` publishes a multi-file bundle: `publish_files({ files: [{ path, content, encoding? }], title, name?, artifact?, base_version?, candidate? })`. `candidate: true` stores a version for review without making it live; see [Propose a change](#propose-a-change). `encoding` is `utf8` (the default) or `base64` for binary files. When `files` has no `artifact.json`, the server writes `{"title":}`. Both return `{ artifact, address, url, version }`. The address never changes across versions. Without `artifact`, the call creates a new artifact owned by the person. With `artifact` (an id or an address), it adds a version to that artifact, and the person must be its owner or an editor. ### Allowed extensions A bundled file's path must be relative, normalised, and use one of these extensions: `.html .htm .css .js .mjs .json .txt .md .csv .xml .svg .png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .ico .woff .woff2 .ttf .otf .mp3 .mp4 .webm .wasm .pdf`. The server sets the content type from the extension, never from the agent. A bundle may hold at most 1,000 files and 25 MiB in total, counting `artifact.json`. It must not repeat a path. ### Secret rules A bundle is refused when any file looks like it holds a secret: - a PEM private key (`-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----`); - a Google service-account key (`"type": "service_account"` with a `private_key`); - a Google API key (`AIza` followed by 35 token characters); - an AWS access key id (`AKIA` followed by 16 upper-case letters or digits); - a GitHub token (`ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `ghr_`, or `github_pat_`); - a Slack token (`xoxa-`, `xoxb-`, `xoxp-`, `xoxr-`, or `xoxs-`); - an OpenAI or Anthropic API key (`sk-` or `sk-ant-` followed by 20 or more key characters). The refusal names the file and the kind of secret, never the value. Do not publish a secret; the person's data comes from their own connections, not from files baked into a bundle. ### `base_version` and conflicts Pass `base_version` when adding a version to an artifact you have read. It must be the version the artifact is current at. If another publish happened first, the call is refused with: ```json { "error": "version-conflict", "current_version": "<id>" } ``` Then call `get_artifact_context` (or `list_versions`) to read the current version, reapply your intended change to those files, and publish again with the new `current_version`. Never overwrite blindly: the version you saw is still in the history, and `rollback` can return to it. ## What an app declares `artifact.json` says what an app uses, and the service allows only what is declared. Every field is optional except `title`. - `providers`: reads one declared source with each viewer's own connection (see [Sources and actions](#sources-and-actions)). An app that declares one is a dashboard. - `personalState: true`: keeps small state for each viewer, read and written with `artifacts.state.personal`. - `sharedState`: keeps small state for everyone with access; `{ "viewersMayWrite": true }` lets viewers change it too. - `collections`: keeps named sets of records, each with its queried fields and its write and delete presets (see [Collections and records](#collections-and-records)). - `actions`: lets the page call a connector method of any class, up to 10 actions. A `send`, `export` or `destructive` method opens the person's confirmation first; a `read` or `write` method needs none (see [Sources and actions](#sources-and-actions)). - `presence: true`: shows who else has the app open. - `deck`: declares slides, fixed at 1600×900 and exportable to Google Slides or PDF. - `widget`: names the HTML file an embedding host draws as the widget (see [Widgets](#widgets)). - `agent`: adds an app agent that answers a viewer's questions about the app, and optionally runs on a schedule (see [App agents](#app-agents)). A plain page declares only a title: ```json { "title": "Q3 review" } ``` A dashboard declares its providers: ```json { "title": "Sales", "providers": [ { "id": "recent", "source": "acme.activity", "params": { "since": "-7d" }, "pick": ["external_id", "kind", "occurred_at", "title"] } ] } ``` An app with slides declares `deck`: ```json { "title": "Q3 review", "deck": { "width": 1600, "height": 900, "slides": [ { "source": "slides/01-cover.html", "title": "Cover" } ] } } ``` An app with personal and shared state declares both: ```json { "title": "Team to-do list", "personalState": true, "sharedState": { "viewersMayWrite": true } } ``` An app may declare any mix of these, and a later version may declare more than an earlier one. ## Dashboards A dashboard reads its providers with each viewer's own connection, never the owner's. No provider data is shared between viewers, and the cache is per viewer. 1. A provider names one source, the params the source is read with, and the fields Studio keeps (`pick`); see [Sources and actions](#sources-and-actions) for the two kinds and their shapes. The first read of a source's service asks the viewer to connect it. When they have not connected, a provider read answers `needs-connection` and the tool returns a `connect_url`; Studio's Connections page shows the status and has a Disconnect control. 2. `publish_dashboard({ files, title, name?, artifact?, base_version? })` publishes a dashboard bundle. Its `artifact.json` must declare at least one provider. A dashboard may mix source providers and BigQuery tiles: ```json { "title": "Sales", "providers": [ { "id": "recent", "source": "acme.activity", "params": { "since": "-7d" }, "pick": ["external_id", "kind", "occurred_at", "title"] }, { "id": "orders", "source": "bigquery", "project": "acme-analytics", "query": "SELECT day, orders FROM `acme-analytics.sales.orders` ORDER BY day", "location": "EU" } ] } ``` `id` starts with a lowercase letter or digit, then lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, and is at most 40 characters and unique. A dashboard declares at most 20 providers, of any kind. Like `publish_files`, the call creates the artifact when none is named and needs agent access `publish` plus the owner or editor role. 3. The dashboard page reads each provider from `GET https://<name>-<suffix>.uc.example.test/.artifact/providers/<id>`. Add `?fresh=1` to read past the 5-minute cache, at most once per 30 seconds per viewer and provider. A declared provider answers a 200 with JSON; an id the dashboard does not declare is 404. Every content-host address in this skill is illustrative: `https://<name>-<suffix>.uc.example.test` stands for an artifact's own address on this environment's content host, not a host to call. Every tool's answer carries the real `url`, so use that. | `status` | Meaning | |---|---| | `ok` | The viewer's own data in `data`, with `updatedAt`. | | `stale` | A transient failure at the source, or the fresh-read rate limit when cached data is expired; the cached `data` and its `updatedAt`. | | `starting` | The viewer's person server is being created; show setup progress and read again shortly. | | `changed` | The source no longer answers the kind `list_connectors` declared; serve the cache as `stale` and tell the person to a …[文件过长——中段 8KB 抽样]… such as boards, notes or bookings. Use shared state instead for a few settings of the whole app, such as a chosen filter or a running total: shared state holds small values, while records are many, each with its own creator and revision, and are read in pages. Records belong in collections, not shared state. A collection is declared in `artifact.json`, and its records are added, read, updated, deleted and queried in fixed shapes. ```json { "title": "Team board", "collections": { "board": { "write": "editors", "delete": "creator-or-owner" } } } ``` A collection name is 1–64 characters: a lowercase letter, then lowercase letters, digits, `_` or `-`. Add a `fields` list to a collection when its queries filter or sort on the record's own values: up to 4 simple field names, kept top-level in each record's body. At most 20 collections per app. `write` is `editors` or `everyone`, and `delete` is `creator-or-owner`, `editors` or `owner`. The owner passes every preset, and an agent has exactly its person's rights: no agent skips a preset, the owner's included. Studio refuses a malformed declaration at publish. The page calls `artifacts.collection(name)`: - `add(body)` → the stored record. - `get(id)` → the record, or rejects `not-found`. - `update(id, body, { expectedRevision, merge })` → the updated record. - `delete(id, { expectedRevision })` → `{ ok: true }`; a missing record is `ok`. - `where(field, "==", value).orderBy(field, direction).limit(n).get()` → `{ records, next }`, one page of a query. - `.after(next)` or `.get({ cursor: next })` → the next page. Every call returns a new query, so a base query can be reused unchanged. A record is `{ id, body, revision, createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt }`. `body` is any JSON object up to 512 KB. `createdBy` is the creator's **app id**, the same value `artifacts.me().id` answers that person, never an email. Compare it with `artifacts.me().id` to tell whether the viewer created a record, and never keep or expect an email. A `createdBy` or `id` inside the body is only body data. A new record starts at revision 1. `update` needs the revision it expects. Without `expectedRevision` it uses the last revision the client saw for that record. A stale write rejects with `ConflictError` carrying `current`, the whole record, and the client never sends your body again on its own: re-read, merge, and try again. Or pass `merge` to retry with the merged body at the current revision, up to 3 attempts in all: ```js await artifacts.collection("board").update(id, { name: mine }, { merge: (theirs, mine) => ({ ...theirs, name: mine.name }), }); ``` ### Records through MCP The page shapes above are what the app's own code uses. To work with records yourself, use the MCP tools, in the app's declared shapes: - `query_artifact_records({ artifact, collection, where?, orderBy?, direction?, limit?, cursor? })` → `{ records, next }`. - `get_artifact_record({ artifact, collection, id })` → `{ record }`. - `write_artifact_record({ artifact, collection, id?, body, expectedRevision? })`: without `id` it adds a record; with `id` it updates one, and `expectedRevision` is required. - `delete_artifact_record({ artifact, collection, id, expectedRevision? })`. - `list_artifact_collections({ artifact })`: every declared collection and every hidden one that still has records, with counts, bytes, `hidden` and `fieldsChanged`. The owner only. - `reindex_artifact_collection({ artifact, collection, cursor? })`: re-indexes older records after a field change. The owner only; see below. Each tool acts as the person whose token it carries, with that person's role and rule presets, and each refusal is a value: `no-access`, `not-declared`, `not-supported` while collections are off, `not-found`, `conflict` with the current record, or `unsupported-query` with a message. An app agent gets `query_records`, `get_record`, `write_record` and `delete_record` when the app declares collections. They are limited to the declared names and act as the viewer who asked, so the same presets apply. ### Queries A query has a fixed shape, so an app never needs its own index: - `where(field, "==", value)` on any of the collection's declared fields, as many or as few as you like. - one `orderBy(field, "asc" | "desc")`: `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, or one declared field. With no sort the page is in `createdAt` ascending order. - `limit(n)` from 1 to 500; the default is 500. - the cursor `next` for the following page. ```js const board = artifacts.collection("board"); const page = await board.where("status", "==", "open").orderBy("points", "desc").limit(50).get(); const more = page.next === null ? { records: [] } : await board.after(page.next).get(); ``` Only `==` is supported, and a field must be declared in the collection's `fields`. Another operator, more than one sort, a value that isn't a string, number or boolean, or a limit outside 1–500 answers `unsupported-query` with a message naming the shapes. A cursor belongs to its artifact, collection and query shape: reusing it on another query answers `invalid-input`. A sort on a declared field never hides a record: every declared field has an indexed value, `null` when the record's value there is missing or is not a string, number or boolean. Ascending order puts those records first and descending order last, and `where(field, "==", value)` never matches `null`. To poll for changes, sort by `updatedAt` descending and read the first page again; records keep their `id`, so merge them into what the page already shows. In a widget every collection call answers `not-supported`. ### After a publish changes fields A publish that drops a collection hides it rather than deleting it — its records stay and still count, and declaring it again brings them back. Only the owner deletes it for good, in Studio. A publish that changes a collection's `fields` applies them to new writes. Older records keep the indexes of the field list they were written for, so a query on a new field can miss them until the collection is reindexed. Run `reindex_artifact_collection` and pass each answer's `next` back as `cursor` until `done` is true. `list_artifact_collections` answers `fieldsChanged: true` until a run that began at the collection's start reaches its end. ## App agents An app can declare an **app agent**: a model that answers a viewer's questions about the app, from the app's own data, or runs on a schedule so a widget keeps itself up to date. Declare one when the person asks for an app they can ask questions of, or a widget that updates itself. Do not declare one for anything plain code can compute: counts, totals, filters and sorting belong in the page. An app agent is one more declaration in `artifact.json`: ```json { "title": "Sales", "providers": [ { "id": "sales", "source": "bigquery", "project": "acme-analytics", "query": "SELECT day, region, amount, owner FROM `acme-analytics.sales.deals`" } ], "agent": { "instructions": "You answer questions about this week's sales. The sales provider holds one row per deal, with day, region, amount and owner. Answer with the numbers from the query, in one short paragraph. If the data does not have a number, say so; never guess." } } ``` `instructions` is 1 to 20,000 characters. Write them for this app, not for a general assistant: - What the app is for, and the question it answers. - Which provider and which state hold what, named by their ids. Say what a column means when its header is unclear. - The tone, and how long a reply should be. - What not to do: not to guess, not to invent numbers, and not to answer about anything outside this app. The app agent acts as the viewer, never as the author. It reads only the app's declared providers, with that viewer's own access; reads the personal and shared state the app declares; sees who is viewing; and may propose one of the app's declared actions. A proposal comes back as a link the person confirms on Studio, and nothing runs before that. It has nothing else: no web, no files, no shell, no other apps, and no …[仅保留首 16KB/中段 8KB/末 8KB]… never the author, nor a workspace's members) from your Gmail when "Send Gmail" is on. It returns `{ change_request, ... }`: the change request's `id`, `artifactId`, `candidateVersionId`, `baseVersionId`, `title`, `description`, `author`, `status` and `createdAt`, and `notified` unless there is nobody to email. When `notified` is false, the reply also adds `reason`, `message` and `link` (the artifact's Studio page) to send instead. Needs agent access `publish` and the owner or editor role. 4. `list_change_requests({ artifact })` lists the artifact's change requests newest first, under both `change_requests` and `changeRequests`, plus `artifact`. Needs agent access `read`. The author can't approve their own request. Merging makes the candidate live only while the current version is still the request's `baseVersionId`; otherwise the request becomes `stale` and a fresh candidate is needed. ## Read an artifact - `resolve_artifact_url({ url })`: resolves an artifact's own URL (any path on its address) to `{ artifact, address }`. Any other URL is `not-found`. - `get_artifact_context({ artifact })`: the title, `declarations`, address, URL, the caller's role, the current version, and its files (`path`, `size`, `content_type`). Read this before editing. - `read_artifact_file({ artifact, path, version? })`: one file of the current or a named version. Text types up to 1 MiB come back as UTF-8 (`encoding: "utf8"`); anything else comes back as base64 (`encoding: "base64"`). The response also carries `path`, `size` and `content_type`. ## Limits to remember - One version: 25 MiB and 1,000 files, counting `artifact.json`. - Publishes: 60 per person per hour. The 61st is refused with `rate-limited` and the response carries `resets_at`. Staged uploads count at finalize. - An access request note: 500 characters. An artifact title and name: 500 characters. - Staged uploads expire one hour after they begin. - An app declares at most 10 actions. - Calls that are not reads: 300 per person per hour. A confirmation expires 10 minutes after it is prepared. - Connector calls: 60 per minute per person per connector, declared reads and live calls together. A `list_connectors` method or source schema above 4 KiB is listed without it. A `try_source` or `try_connector` answer above 32 KiB is cut. - A source provider's `params` is at most 16 KiB serialized, and its `pick` keeps 1 to 50 paths of 1 to 200 characters each. A relative time is at most 366 days either way. - A deck has 1 to 100 slides, each 1600×900. A slide title: 200 characters. - A BigQuery provider: a `SELECT` query of 1 to 10,000 characters, at most 1 GB scanned per run, and a project id of 6 to 30 characters. - Exports: 20 per person per hour, PDF and Google Slides together. The 21st is refused with `rate-limited`. - A PDF export is kept for 24 hours. A deck image link works once and expires after 10 minutes. - Personal state: 1 MB per person per artifact. - Shared state: 10 MB per artifact, 1,000 keys, and 256 KB for one value. - Feed writes to shared state: 60 per hour per sink grant, and at most 20 sink grants per artifact. A feed name: 1 to 80 characters. A pending sink grant expires 7 days after it is created. - `artifacts.ask` (or its alias `artifacts.askJelly`): text of 1 to 2,000 characters. - An app agent's `instructions`: 1 to 20,000 characters. One message, or a schedule's prompt: 1 to 4,000 characters. Messages: 20 per person per minute. - An app agent run: 60 seconds, 20 tool calls and at most $0.50. The AI budget is $10 per person per day, across all apps. Conversations are deleted 60 days after their last message. One message is 1 to 4,000 characters; a conversation's title is its first message, cut to 80 characters. - Widget layout checks: 30 per person per hour, at most 12 shots per check. - Presence leases last 30 seconds; a heartbeat every 10 seconds, and one within 5 seconds of the last is ignored. At most 200 people are listed, and a lease expired for more than an hour is removed. - A workspace: name 1 to 100 characters, 20 created per person and 200 members. - A change request: title 1 to 200 characters, description up to 5,000. ## Tool reference | Tool | Purpose | Needs | |---|---|---| | `auth_status` | Who the agent acts for and its `agentAccess`. | any agent | | `publish_html` | Create a page, or add a version with one `index.html`. | publish | | `publish_files` | Create a page, app or deck, or add a version, from a bundle. | publish | | `publish_dashboard` | Create a dashboard, or add a version, declaring its providers. | publish | | `write_artifact_state` | Write an app's personal state, or shared state through a feed's approved grant. | publish | | `validate_artifact_app` | Check a bundle without publishing it. | read | | `validate_deck_layout` | Check a deck's slides at 1600×900 and report layout problems. | read | | `check_widget_layout` | Render an app's widget file, or the app itself, at the configured widget sizes, with each screenshot and its layout problems. | read | | `export_pdf` | Export a deck as a PDF for the exporting person, kept 24 hours. | read | | `export_slides` | Export a deck to a new Google Slides file in the person's Drive. | read, `slides.write` connection | | `inspect_bigquery_query` | Dry-run a BigQuery SELECT: statement type, bytes, columns and a sample. | read | | `list_connectors` | List the caller's connectors, their services and sources, and their methods with classes and input schemas. | read | | `try_source` | Read one source as the caller's own person, exactly as a provider will. | read | | `try_connector` | Call one connector `read` method as the caller's own person and read its answer. | read | | `read_artifact_provider` | Read a provider's data from an artifact with the caller's own access. | read | | `ask_app_agent` | Ask an app's agent a question, as the person, and read its reply. | read | | `begin_artifact_upload` | Declare the files of a staged upload. | publish | | `write_artifact_upload_chunk` | Send one chunk of a staged file. | publish | | `finalize_artifact_upload` | Check every # toqan artifacts for OpenCode

One OpenCode plugin that gives an agent toqan artifacts: Studio's tools, the
agent skill, and default permissions that ask the person before anything is
shared, deleted, stopped or resumed.

Requires OpenCode `>=2.2.3 <2.3.0`.

## Install

The plugin is published on npm as `@joe-broadhead/opencode-artifacts`. Add it
to `plugins` in `opencode.json(c)`; OpenCode downloads it on start:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": ["@joe-broadhead/opencode-artifacts"]
}
```

To stay on one version, pin it: `"@joe-broadhead/opencode-artifacts@0.2.2"`.

To use another Studio, add options:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "@joe-broadhead/opencode-artifacts",
      "options": { "studioUrl": "https://studio.example.com" }
    }
  ]
}
```

`studioUrl` defaults to the dev Studio, `https://artifacts.dev.toqanjelly.ai`, while PM
testing runs there. Set it to `https://artifacts.toqanjelly.ai` for prod. It
must be an https origin. Plain `http://` is accepted only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and
`[::1]`, for a Studio on the same machine. Loading the plugin makes no network
call.

A host that can mint tokens for a named resource sets `identityAccessor` to
the name it registers its identity accessor under:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "@joe-broadhead/opencode-artifacts",
      "options": { "identityAccessor": "example.identity" }
    }
  ]
}
```

When it is set and the host registers an accessor under that name, the plugin
looks up `globalThis[Symbol.for("<value>")]` on each tool call and asks it for
a token for the `artifacts` resource, always passing the tool call's session
id, so the token names the person speaking. That token goes to Studio instead of
the `/connect` credential, and while the accessor is there it is the only
credential used: if it answers no token, refuses or fails, the tool reports `AUTH_REQUIRED`, because
the host's own sign-in is needed. A stored `/connect` credential belongs to the
agent's owner, so it is never spent for a host-relayed call, and a member never
acts as the owner. If Studio refuses the host's token, the plugin asks the same
accessor again for the same session and retries; a second refusal, as after a
revoked trusted issuer, reports `AUTH_REQUIRED`. The plugin logs no token and
caches nothing beyond what the accessor itself caches.

The `/connect` credential is used only when there is no accessor to ask: the
option is unset, or it names an accessor the host does not offer. The option is
the host's to set: stock OpenCode leaves it out, and the plugin then signs in
only through `/connect`.

## Sign in

1. Run `/connect` and choose **Artifacts**.
2. OpenCode opens Studio's sign-in page in the browser. Sign in with your
   verified account.
3. Studio's consent page asks what this agent may do. Pick one:

   | Access | What the agent may do |
   |---|---|
   | **Read** | view artifacts and their data |
   | **Publish** | read, plus create artifacts and publish versions |
   | **Manage** (default) | publish, plus share, delete, stop and resume |

   The level can be changed later by revoking the agent on Studio's Agent
   access page and connecting again.
4. Come back to OpenCode. The credential is stored in OpenCode's own credential
   store; the plugin never writes a token to a file.

Studio registers the plugin as a public OAuth client each time you sign in, with
a loopback redirect (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback`), PKCE (S256), and the
scopes `openid profile email offline_access artifacts:read artifacts:publish
artifacts:manage`. Studio asks for all three artifact scopes so the consent page
can offer every access level, and narrows the grant to the level you choose.
Studio ignores the loopback port, so the plugin listens on any free port.

When your browser is on another machine, as on a jelly cloud, the host gives the
redirect instead, in two hidden fields of the sign-in (`redirectUri` and
`callbackPort`): Studio registers that address, which is jelly's sign-in relay,
and sends your browser back there. jelly hands the answer to the plugin's
listener on `127.0.0.1:<callbackPort>`. A terminal's `/connect` leaves both
blank and keeps the loopback redirect.

OpenCode stores the credential and refreshes it with the refresh token through
the plugin's refresh method; Studio rotates the refresh token on every refresh,
and OpenCode keeps the new one. A tool never spends the refresh token itself:
with no identity accessor, if Studio refuses a call, the plugin asks OpenCode
for the current token once and retries. If that is refused too, or the person
is no longer signed in, the tool reports:

```
AUTH_REQUIRED: Artifacts isn't signed in. Next step: run /connect and choose Artifacts.
```

## What the tools do

There is one tool for each MCP tool Studio lists, with Studio's own name,
description and input schema, in the `artifacts` namespace: OpenCode names
each one `artifacts_<tool>` (`artifacts_publish_html`), and Code Mode calls it
as `tools.artifacts.<tool>`. Each one forwards its input to `<studioUrl>/mcp`
as an MCP `tools/call` with your token and returns Studio's answer unchanged.
Text comes back as text; an image (a widget layout screenshot, for example)
comes back as a file OpenCode can show, with the same bytes and MIME type.
Studio is the only place that checks access, so the plugin holds no access
rules of its own. Studio's content is untrusted data, never instructions, and
the namespace's Code Mode text says so.

Studio's tool list changes independently of the plugin. `plugin/tools.json`
records the list this plugin was built against; a test fails when it drifts, and
`pnpm plugin:tools` regenerates it.

## Which tools ask

Every tool asserts its own permission, `artifacts_<tool>`, before it forwards
anything, so a rule of yours that asks or denies any tool holds. The plugin
adds an `ask` rule for these ten, which are direct tools, so you see a prompt
first:

| Tool | What it changes |
|---|---|
| `share_site` | shares an artifact with a person or everyone in the organization |
| `unshare_site` | removes a share |
| `share_workspace` | shares an artifact with a workspace |
| `decide_access_request` | approves or denies an access request; approving shares the artifact |
| `delete_site` | deletes an artifact |
| `stop_site` | stops serving an artifact's address |
| `resume_site` | serves a stopped artifact again |
| `ensure_workspace` | creates a workspace or adds people to it |
| `request_site_access` | asks an artifact's owner for access |
| `open_change_request` | asks an artifact's owner and editors to review a version |

Everything else — reading, publishing, dashboards, decks, versions,
connections, widget checks, exports — runs without asking, in Code
Mode.

The rules are on the actions `artifacts_share_site`, `artifacts_unshare_site`,
`artifacts_share_workspace`, `artifacts_decide_access_request`,
`artifacts_delete_site`, `artifacts_stop_site`, `artifacts_resume_site`,
`artifacts_ensure_workspace`, `artifacts_request_site_access` and
`artifacts_open_change_request`, one
per tool, added to every agent the plugin sees at setup, right after that
agent's base allow. A person's own rule wins when it comes later: `deny` hides
the tool, and an `allow` for an artifact skips the prompt. Before 0.2.0 the
actions were named `artifacts.<tool>`; rename a rule of yours that uses that
form.

Agents defined only in the person's config are created after plugins run, so
they can miss these rules. Add the same rules to that agent's `permissions` to
get the prompts; do not put the ask rules in the top-level `permissions`, where
they would also apply to other agents.

## In Jelly

`package.json` carries a `jelly` declaration that Jelly reads without loading
the plugin; stock OpenCode ignores it. [docs/jelly.md](docs/jelly.md) says how
Jelly uses it. `test/jelly.test.ts` checks it with the shared kit
(`test/support/jelly-kit.ts`), and `npm run check` (`scripts/check-copies.mjs`)
fails when the kit differs from the copy every plugin in this family carries.

## The skill

`skills/jelly-artifacts/SKILL.md` is the same file Studio serves at
`/skill.md`, copied by `pnpm plugin:skill`. It is auto-invoked, so the agent
reads it whenever the person wants a page, dashboard, deck, app, game or Jelly
widget made, changed or shared — and publishes it with toqan artifacts rather
than as the chat app's own artifact.

## Troubleshooting

- **`AUTH_REQUIRED`** — run `/connect`, choose Artifacts, and finish the
  sign-in.
- **The tools are missing** — check that the `plugins` entry is
  `@joe-broadhead/opencode-artifacts` (or, for a local build, the `plugin`
  directory itself, with `dist/` compiled), and that OpenCode is 2.2.x.
  `/reload` picks up a config change.
- **`CONFIG_INVALID: studioUrl ...`** — the option must be a bare origin with
  no path, such as `https://artifacts.toqanjelly.ai`. Plain `http://` works
  only on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`.
- **`CONFIG_INVALID: identityAccessor ...`** — the option must be the
  non-empty name the host registers its accessor under. Remove it when no host
  sets one.
- **`MOVED: Studio has moved to <address>`** — the Studio you use answered
  that it now lives at `<address>`. Set `studioUrl` to that address (or remove
  the option, when the message says the default is that address), then run
  `/connect`: a sign-in belongs to the address it was made at.
- **A tool reports an HTTP status** — Studio answered, but not with a tool
  result. Check `/connect` first, then Studio's own status.

## Develop locally

Build the plugin from this repository and point `plugins` at the `plugin`
directory with an absolute path:

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm plugin:build                # refresh tools.json and the skill from Studio
pnpm --dir plugin compile        # compile src/ to dist/
```

```jsonc
{ "plugins": ["/absolute/path/to/artifacts/plugin"] }
```

OpenCode loads `exports["."]`, which is `./dist/index.js`, and reads
`tools.json` and `skills/jelly-artifacts/SKILL.md` next to it. Run
`pnpm --dir plugin compile` again after changing `src/`. `dist/` is not
committed.

## Release a new version

`tools.json` and the skill are copies of Studio taken at build time, so
release a new version when Studio adds or changes a tool, when the skill
changes, or when the plugin's own code changes. A published version can never
be replaced; every change is a new version number.

| Change | Bump |
|---|---|
| A fix | `patch` (0.2.0 → 0.2.1) |
| A new or changed Studio tool, a skill change, a new option | `minor` (0.2.1 → 0.3.0) |
| A change that breaks existing configs, or a new OpenCode host range | `major` |

1. In a pull request, run `pnpm plugin:build`, bump `version` in
   `plugin/package.json`, add a `## [x.y.z] - date` entry to
   `plugin/CHANGELOG.md`, and declare any new tool in the `jelly` section
   (`test/jelly.test.ts` fails until you do). Merge it once `check` is green.
2. Tag that commit on `main` as `v<version>` and push the tag. Nothing else
   releases.
3. `release-plugin.yml` checks that the tag matches the version, runs the
   plugin's tests and `npm run check`, packs the plugin, and waits for approval
   in the `release` environment. Once approved, it publishes the tarball to npm
   with trusted publishing. This repository is private, and npm makes no
   provenance for a private repository, so it publishes without.

`npm pack --dry-run` in `plugin/` shows the file list: `dist`, `assets/icon.svg`,
`skills`, `tools.json`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`.

All notable changes to the toqan artifacts OpenCode plugin are documented here. The format follows [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and versions follow [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [0.6.0] - 2026-11-18

### Added

- `query_artifact_records` reads one page of an app collection in a fixed shape: `==` on any declared field, one sort by `createdAt`, `updatedAt` or a declared field, a limit of 1–500 and a cursor for the next page.
- `get_artifact_record` reads one record by id.
- `write_artifact_record` adds a record, or updates one at the revision last read, which is required for an update.
- `delete_artifact_record` deletes one record, optionally at the revision last read; a missing record is still deleted.
- `reindex_artifact_collection` re-indexes a collection's older records after a publish changed its declared fields. The owner runs it and passes each answer's `next` back until `done` is true.
- `list_artifact_collections` lists an app's collections for its owner, with record counts, bytes, hidden ones and any reindex still due.

### Changed

- The skill teaches when to use collections rather than shared state, the rule presets, the record tools and their MCP names, the query shapes and `unsupported-query`, that `createdBy` is the viewer's app id, that a publish hides a dropped collection, and the reindex loop. App agents get `query_records`, `get_record`, `write_record` and `delete_record` for a declared collection, acting as the viewer.

## [0.5.0] - 2026-11-17

### Added

- `get_artifact_bundle` returns one version of an app as a bundle — every file plus the runtime its page loads (`/.artifact/client.js`, the brand stylesheet and fonts) — so an embedding host can draw it in a sealed frame (ADR 0049, `docs/host-bridge.md`).
- `read_artifact_state` reads the person's own personal state for an app, the counterpart of `write_artifact_state`'s personal write.
- `call_artifact_action` runs one action an app declares, as the person, for an embedding host only: a class that needs a confirmation answers `needs-confirmation` with a plain description, the host asks the person in its own UI, then sends the same call again with `confirmation`. Any caller that is not a host relaying with a trusted issuer's token is refused `needs-host`. Declared `ask`.

### Changed

- The skill teaches apps that work both in a browser and as a widget: what works in a widget (data, personal state, declared actions, Ask, `artifacts.host`), what doesn't (shared state, presence, the app agent), and `artifacts.ask` with `askJelly` kept as an alias. It names no host; the plugin writes its own `studioUrl` into the skill and tool descriptions when it loads them.
